s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and mass with acute exacerbation
salient_findings: Palpable, movable mass in the upper abdomen
Large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum on ultrasound
Large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall on endoscopy
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
Insidious upper abdominal pain unrelated to food ingestion
Nausea
Episode of intense acute abdominal pain
No hematemesis or melena
Untreated dyslipidemia
Well-controlled hypertension on methyldopa
Smoker of ten cigarettes per day
No family history of cancer
Normal physical examination except for abdominal mass
Normal complete blood count without anemia
Abdominal ultrasound showed large echogenic mass in gastric antrum
Endoscopy revealed large submucosal bulging mass in posterior gastric wall
Biopsy attempts failed to sample submucosal mass
Ulcer biopsies showed only necrotic mucosa
Contrast-enhanced CT showed well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass arising from posterior gastric wall

Gastric desmoplastic small round cell tumor

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Large submucosal bulging mass in posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas and fat-tissue attenuation on CT

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement and trabecular architecture on CT, consistent with a benign fatty tumor

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large submucosal mass with smooth borders and homogeneous appearance on CT, consistent with a benign smooth muscle tumor

shortlist.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcerated areas and large mass in gastric antrum, although less likely given the fat-tissue attenuation on CT

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement and trabecular architecture on CT, although less common than other options

raw.rationale: The lesion had fat-tissue attenuation on CT, which is consistent with a lipoma, a benign tumor composed of fat tissue.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors often have a more heterogeneous appearance on imaging and may have a higher risk of malignancy.

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are typically solid and have a more uniform appearance on imaging, without the characteristic fat-tissue attenuation seen in this case.

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Gastric adenocarcinoma would likely cause more significant symptoms such as weight loss, and the imaging findings would more likely show an irregular, ulcerated mass rather than a well-defined, homogeneous mass.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are malignant tumors that would likely have a more aggressive appearance on imaging, with necrosis, hemorrhage, or invasion into surrounding structures, which is not seen in this case.
